events.label: Holmes and Watson remain indoors all day
Holmes conducts chemical investigations
A test-tube breaks and ends Holmes's research
Holmes invites Watson to take a ramble through London

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: What do you say to a ramble through London?

events.label: Holmes and Watson stroll through London
Holmes and Watson return to Baker Street
A brougham waits at the door
Holmes remarks that the visitor is a doctor's general practitioner

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Hum! A doctor's—general practitioner, I perceive. Not been long in practice, but has had a good deal to do. Come to consult us, I fancy! Lucky we came back!

events.label: Holmes and Watson enter their sanctum
The doctor rises from a chair by the fire
The doctor lays his hand on the mantelpiece
Doctor Percy Trevelyan introduces himself to Holmes and gives his address

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: My name is Doctor Percy Trevelyan, and I live at 403, Brook Street.

events.label: Holmes asks Trevelyan about the obscure nervous lesions monograph

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Are you not the author of a monograph upon obscure nervous lesions?

events.label: Trevelyan responds that his work was known and that his publishers reported poor sales

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: I so seldom hear of the work that I thought it was quite dead. My publishers gave me a most discouraging account of its sale. You are yourself, I presume, a medical man?

events.label: Holmes says he is a retired Army surgeon

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: A retired Army surgeon.

events.label: Trevelyan explains his medical interests and the recent disturbance at his house

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: My own hobby has always been nervous disease. I should wish to make it an absolute specialty, but, of course, a man must take what he can get at first. This, however, is beside the question, Mr. Sherlock Holmes, and I quite appreciate how valuable your time is. The fact is that a very singular train of events has occurred recently at my house in Brook Street, and to-night they came to such a head that I felt it was quite impossible for me to wait another hour before asking for your advice and assistance.

events.label: Holmes sits down and lights his pipe
Holmes invites Trevelyan to give a detailed account of the disturbance

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You are very welcome to both. Pray let me have a detailed account of what the circumstances are which have disturbed you.

events.label: Trevelyan says he will explain the matter and begins with his college career

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: One or two of them are so trivial, but the matter is so inexplicable, and the recent turn which it has taken is so elaborate, that I shall lay it all before you, and you shall judge what is essential and what is not. I am compelled, to begin with, to say something of my own college career.

events.label: Trevelyan describes his university and research career and mentions winning a prize

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: I am a London University man, and my student career was considered by my professors to be a very promising one. After I had graduated I continued to devote myself to research, occupying a minor position in King's College Hospital, and I was fortunate enough to excite considerable interest by my research into the pathology of catalepsy, and finally to win the Bruce Pinkerton prize and medal by the monograph on nervous lesions to which your friend has just alluded. There was a general impression at that time that a distinguished career lay before me.

events.label: Trevelyan explains that lack of capital hindered his career

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: But the one great stumbling-block lay in my want of capital. As you will readily understand, a specialist who aims high is compelled to start in one of a dozen streets in the Cavendish Square quarter, all of which entail enormous rents and furnishing expenses. Besides this preliminary outlay, he must be prepared to keep himself for some years, and to hire a presentable carriage and horse. To do this was quite beyond my power, and I could only hope that by economy I might in ten years' time save enough to enable me to put up my plate.

events.label: Trevelyan says an unexpected incident opened a new prospect

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: Suddenly, however, an unexpected incident opened up quite a new prospect to me.

events.label: Blessington visits Trevelyan's room and begins business immediately
Percy Trevelyan asks Holmes to answer frankly

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: Answer me frankly, for you will find it to your interest to do so.

events.label: Percy Trevelyan asks Holmes about bad habits and drink

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: Any bad habits? Not drawn towards drink, eh?

events.label: Percy Trevelyan remarks on his own proposal to start Holmes in Brook Street

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: It's the old story. More in your brains than in your pocket, eh? What would you say if I were to start you in Brook Street?

events.label: Percy Trevelyan offers to invest in Holmes

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: It's for my sake, not for yours. I'll be perfectly frank with you, and if it suits you it will suit me very well. I have a few thousands to invest, d'ye see, and I think I'll sink them in you.

events.label: Percy Trevelyan explains the business arrangement

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: I'll tell you. I'll take the house, furnish it, pay the maids, and run the whole place. All you have to do is just to wear out your chair in the consulting-room. I'll let you have pocket-money and everything. Then you hand over to me three quarters of what you earn, and you keep the other quarter for yourself.

events.label: Percy Trevelyan describes Blessington approaching him with a proposal
Percy Trevelyan moves into the house and starts practice
Blessington comes to live with Percy Trevelyan as a resident patient
Blessington uses the consulting-room to inspect accounts and take proceeds
Blessington speaks of a burglary and urges stronger security

communicates.speaker: blessington
communicates.content: Some weeks ago a burglary had been committed in the West End, and we should add stronger bolts to our windows and doors before another day passes.

events.label: Blessington becomes restless and watches the windows
Percy Trevelyan questions Blessington and then drops the subject
The narrator receives an anonymous letter
The letter asks Dr. Percy Trevelyan for medical assistance

communicates.speaker: anonymous_russian_nobleman
communicates.content: A Russian nobleman resident in England would be glad to avail himself of the professional assistance of Dr. Percy Trevelyan. He has been for some years a victim to cataleptic attacks. He proposes to call at about quarter past six to-morrow evening if Dr. Trevelyan will make it convenient to be at home.

events.label: The page admits the patient into the consulting-room
The young man helps the elderly man to a chair
The young man explains that the elderly man is his father and asks to stay out of the consultation

communicates.speaker: anonymous_young_man
communicates.content: You will excuse my coming in, doctor. This is my father, and his health is a matter of the most overwhelming importance to me. Not for the world. It is more painful to me than I can express. If I were to see my father in one of these dreadful seizures I am convinced that I should never survive it. My own nervous system is an exceptionally sensitive one. With your permission, I will remain in the waiting-room while you go into my father's case.

events.label: Percy Trevelyan assents and the young man withdraws
Trevelyan consults the patient and takes notes
The patient becomes rigid in cataleptic seizure
Trevelyan examines the patient's pulse, temperature, muscles, and reflexes
Trevelyan leaves to fetch nitrite of amyl from the laboratory
Trevelyan returns to the consulting-room and finds the patient gone
Trevelyan runs to the waiting-room and finds the young man gone
Trevelyan speaks about the page and the mystery

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: My page who admits patients is a new boy and by no means quick. He waits downstairs, and runs up to show patients out when I ring the consulting-room bell. He had heard nothing, and the affair remained a complete mystery.

events.label: Mr. Blessington comes in from his walk
The Russian and his son arrive in the consulting-room
The patient apologizes for his abrupt departure and explains his clouded memory after attacks

communicates.speaker: anonymous_russian_nobleman
communicates.content: I owe you a great many apologies for my abrupt departure yesterday, doctor. The fact is that when I recover from these attacks my mind is always very clouded as to all that has gone before. I woke up in a strange room, as it seemed to me, and made my way out into the street in a sort of dazed way when you were absent.

events.label: The son explains why he thought the consultation had ended

communicates.speaker: anonymous_young_man
communicates.content: Seeing my father pass the door of the waiting-room, I naturally thought that the consultation had come to an end. It was not until we had reached home that I began to realize the true state of affairs.

events.label: The doctor resumes the consultation and prescribes treatment
Blessington enters, goes upstairs, rushes down, and bursts into the consulting-room in panic
Blessington demands whether anyone has been in his room and cries out in alarm

communicates.speaker: blessington
communicates.content: Been in my room? No one! It's a lie! Come up and look!

events.label: The doctor goes upstairs with Blessington and sees footprints on the carpet
The doctor reasons that an intruder ascended to the resident patient's room while he was busy
Blessington becomes highly agitated and suggests consulting Holmes

communicates.speaker: blessington
communicates.content: It was his suggestion that I should come round to you, and of course I at once saw the propriety of it, for certainly the incident is a very singular one, though he appears to completely overrate its importance. If you would only come back with me in my brougham, you would at least be able to soothe him, though I can hardly hope that you will be able to explain this remarkable occurrence.

events.label: Holmes listens to the doctor's narrative with intense attention
Holmes leaves with the doctor and Watson and arrives at Dr. Trevelyan's residence
A page admits the visitors and they begin ascending the stair
A hidden man warns the others not to come nearer with a pistol

communicates.speaker: anonymous_young_man
communicates.content: I have a pistol. I give you my word that I'll fire if you come any nearer.

events.label: Dr. Trevelyan addresses Blessington by name

communicates.speaker: doctor
communicates.content: This really grows outrageous, Mr. Blessington.

events.label: The hidden man identifies the doctor and asks about the other men

communicates.speaker: anonymous_young_man
communicates.content: Oh, then it is you, doctor. But those other gentlemen, are they what they pretend to be?

events.label: The hidden man scrutinizes the visitors from the darkness and allows them to come up

communicates.speaker: anonymous_young_man
communicates.content: Yes, yes, it's all right. You can come up, and I am sorry if my precautions have annoyed you.

events.label: The man relights the stair gas and reveals himself
Blessington greets Holmes and explains his situation

communicates.speaker: blessington
communicates.content: Good-evening, Mr. Holmes. I am sure I am very much obliged to you for coming round. No one ever needed your advice more than I do. I suppose that Dr. Trevelyan has told you of this most unwarrantable intrusion into my rooms.

events.label: Holmes asks Blessington about the two men who intrude on him

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Who are these two men Mr. Blessington, and why do they wish to molest you?

events.label: Blessington refuses to answer Holmes's question directly

communicates.speaker: blessington
communicates.content: Well, well, of course it is hard to say that. You can hardly expect me to answer that, Mr. Holmes.

events.label: Blessington leads Holmes into his bedroom and points out a black box
Holmes rejects Blessington's attempted deception and leaves

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I cannot possibly advise you if you try to deceive me. Good-night, Dr. Trevelyan. My advice to you, sir, is to speak the truth.

events.label: Holmes and Watson walk home from the house
Holmes comments that the visit was a fool's errand and analyzes the intruders

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Sorry to bring you out on such a fool's errand, Watson. It is an interesting case, too, at the bottom of it. I can make little of it. Well, it is quite evident that there are two men—more, perhaps, but at least two—who are determined for some reason to get at this fellow Blessington. I have no doubt in my mind that both on the first and on the second occasion that young man penetrated to Blessington's room, while his confederate, by an ingenious device, kept the doctor from interfering.

events.label: Holmes dismisses the catalepsy as a fraudulent imitation

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: A fraudulent imitation, Watson, though I should hardly dare to hint as much to our specialist. It is a very easy complaint to imitate. I have done it myself.

events.label: Holmes explains why Blessington was absent and why the men chose the hour

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: By the purest chance Blessington was out on each occasion. Their reason for choosing so unusual an hour for a consultation was obviously to insure that there should be no other patient in the waiting-room. It just happened, however, that this hour coincided with Blessington's constitutional, which seems to show that they were not very well acquainted with his daily routine. Of course, if they had been merely after plunder they would at least have made some attempt to search for it. Besides, I can read in a man's eye when it is his own skin that he is frightened for. It is inconceivable that this fellow could have made two such vindictive enemies as these appear to be without knowing of it. I hold it, therefore, to be certain that he does know who these men are, and that for reasons of his own he suppresses it. It is just possible that to-morrow may find him in a more communicative mood.

events.label: Watson suggests an alternative explanation for the catalepsy story

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: Is there not one alternative, grotesquely improbable, no doubt, but still just conceivable? Might the whole story of the cataleptic Russian and his son be a concoction of Dr. Trevelyan's, who has, for his own purposes, been in Blessington's rooms?

events.label: Holmes says he corroborated the doctor's tale from footprints and shoes

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It was one of the first solutions which occurred to me, but I was soon able to corroborate the doctor's tale. This young man has left prints upon the stair-carpet which made it quite superfluous for me to ask to see those which he had made in the room. When I tell you that his shoes were square-toed instead of being pointed like Blessington's, and were quite an inch and a third longer than the doctor's, you will acknowledge that there can be no doubt as to his individuality. But we may sleep on it now, for I shall be surprised if we do not hear something further from Brook Street in the morning.

events.label: Holmes appears at Watson's bedside and calls for the brougham

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: There's a brougham waiting for us, Watson. The Brook Street business. Tragic, but ambiguous. Our friend, the doctor, was hard put to it when he wrote this. Come along, my dear fellow, for it's an urgent call.

events.label: Holmes and Watson return to the physician's house
The doctor meets Holmes and Watson with horror

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: Oh, such a business!

events.label: The doctor announces that Blessington has committed suicide

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: Blessington has committed suicide! Yes, he hanged himself during the night.

events.label: The doctor says police are already upstairs and the event has shaken him

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: I really hardly know what I am doing. The police are already upstairs. It has shaken me most dreadfully.

events.label: The doctor explains when he found Blessington hanging and how he died

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: He has a cup of tea taken in to him early every morning. When the maid entered, about seven, there the unfortunate fellow was hanging in the middle of the room. He had tied his cord to the hook on which the heavy lamp used to hang, and he had jumped off from the top of the very box that he showed us yesterday.

events.label: Holmes asks to go upstairs and inspect the matter

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: With your permission, I should like to go upstairs and look into the matter.

events.label: Holmes, Watson, and the doctor ascend upstairs
They enter the bedroom and find Blessington dead
Lanner greets Holmes and says he is delighted to see him

communicates.speaker: lanner
communicates.content: Ah, Mr. Holmes, I am delighted to see you.

events.label: Holmes asks Lanner about the events leading to the affair

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Good-morning, Lanner, you won't think me an intruder, I am sure. Have you heard of the events which led up to this affair?

events.label: Lanner says he has heard something of the events

communicates.speaker: lanner
communicates.content: Yes, I heard something of them.

events.label: Holmes asks Lanner for his opinion

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Have you formed any opinion?

events.label: Lanner describes the case and the body

communicates.speaker: lanner
communicates.content: As far as I can see, the man has been driven out of his senses by fright. The bed has been well slept in, you see. There's his impression deep enough. It's about five in the morning, you know, that suicides are most common. That would be about his time for hanging himself. It seems to have been a very deliberate affair.

events.label: Watson states that the man has been dead about three hours

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: I should say that he has been dead about three hours, judging by the rigidity of the muscles.

events.label: Holmes asks whether anything peculiar was noticed in the room

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Noticed anything peculiar about the room?

events.label: Lanner reports objects found in the room

communicates.speaker: lanner
communicates.content: Found a screw-driver and some screws on the wash-hand stand. Seems to have smoked heavily during the night, too. Here are four cigar-ends that I picked out of the fireplace.

events.label: Holmes asks whether the cigar-holder has been found

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Hum! have you got his cigar-holder?

events.label: Lanner says he has seen no cigar-holder

communicates.speaker: lanner
communicates.content: No, I have seen none.

events.label: Holmes asks about the cigar-case

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: His cigar-case, then?

events.label: Lanner says the cigar-case was in the coat-pocket

communicates.speaker: lanner
communicates.content: Yes, it was in his coat-pocket.

events.label: Holmes opens the cigar-case and smells the cigar inside
Holmes identifies the cigar types and their features
Holmes examines the four cigar-ends with his pocket-lens
Holmes states that two cigar-ends were smoked from a holder and two without

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Two of these have been smoked from a holder and two without.

events.label: Holmes states that the cigar-ends were cut or bitten

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Two have been cut by a not very sharp knife, and two have had the ends bitten off by a set of excellent teeth.

events.label: Holmes declares the death to be murder rather than suicide

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: This is no suicide, Mr. Lanner. It is a very deeply planned and cold-blooded murder.

events.label: The inspector exclaims that Holmes's claim is impossible

communicates.speaker: lanner
communicates.content: Impossible!

events.label: Holmes asks why someone would murder a man by hanging him

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: And why? Why should any one murder a man in so clumsy a fashion as by hanging him?

events.label: Holmes and Lanner discuss how the perpetrators entered

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: How could they get in? Through the front door. It was barred in the morning. Then it was barred after them. How do you know?

events.label: Holmes says he saw their traces and asks to inspect the door

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I saw their traces. Excuse me a moment, and I may be able to give you some further information about it.

events.label: Holmes inspects the room and the body, then the body is cut down and laid under a sheet
Dr. Trevelyan draws a large coil from under the bed
Dr. Trevelyan explains the rope was kept beside him for escape from fire

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: He was morbidly nervous of fire, and always kept this beside him, so that he might escape by the window in case the stairs were burning.

events.label: Holmes takes the photograph of Blessington from the mantelpiece
Holmes states that three men were in it

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: There were three of them in it: the young man, the old man, and a third, to whose identity I have no clue.

events.label: Holmes states that the first two men masqueraded as the Russian count and his son

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: The first two, I need hardly remark, are the same who masqueraded as the Russian count and his son, so we can give a very full description of them.

events.label: Holmes states that the men were admitted by a confederate inside the house

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: They were admitted by a confederate inside the house.

events.label: Holmes advises arresting the page

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: it would be to arrest the page, who, as I understand, has only recently come into your service, Doctor.

events.label: Dr. Trevelyan says the page cannot be found and the maid and cook have searched for him

communicates.speaker: percy_trevelyan
communicates.content: The young imp cannot be found; the maid and the cook have just been searching for him.

events.label: Holmes states that the page played a part in the drama

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: He has played a not unimportant part in this drama.

events.label: Holmes states that the three men ascended the stairs on tiptoe

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: The three men having ascended the stairs, which they did on tiptoe, the elder man first, the younger man second, and the unknown man in the rear.

events.label: Holmes states that the men went to Blessington's room and found the door locked

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: They ascended, then, to Mr. Blessington's room, the door of which they found to be locked.

events.label: The men force the key round with a wire
Holmes states that the men gag Mr. Blessington on entering the room

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: On entering the room their first proceeding must have been to gag Mr. Blessington.

events.label: Holmes states that a consultation is held after Blessington is secured

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Having secured him, it is evident to me that a consultation of some sort was held. Probably it was something in the nature of a judicial proceeding.

events.label: Holmes states that the older man sits in the wicker chair and uses the cigar-holder

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: The older man sat in that wicker chair; it was he who used the cigar-holder.

events.label: Holmes states that the younger man sits by the chest of drawers and knocks ash off against it

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: The younger man sat over yonder; he knocked his ash off against the chest of drawers.

events.label: Holmes states that the third man paces up and down

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: The third fellow paced up and down.

events.label: Holmes states that Blessington sits upright in the bed

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Blessington, I think, sat upright in the bed, but of that I cannot be absolutely certain.

events.label: Holmes states that the men hang Blessington

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: it ended by their taking Blessington and hanging him.

events.label: Holmes states that the men brought a block or pulley to serve as a gallows

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: The matter was so prearranged that it is my belief that they brought with them some sort of block or pulley which might serve as a gallows. That screw-driver and those screws were, as I conceive, for fixing it up.

events.label: Holmes states that the men avoid trouble by using the hook

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Seeing the hook, however they naturally saved themselves the trouble.

events.label: Holmes states that the men make off and their confederate bars the door behind them

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Having finished their work they made off, and the door was barred behind them by their confederate.

events.label: The inspector hurries away to make inquiries about the page
Holmes and Watson return to Baker Street for breakfast
The visitors arrive at the appointed time
Holmes arrives late
Holmes reports that he has identified the men

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You have got them! Well, at least I have got their identity. This so-called Blessington is, as I expected, well known at headquarters, and so are his assailants. Their names are Biddle, Hayward, and Moffat.

events.label: The inspector identifies the gang

communicates.speaker: inspector
communicates.content: The Worthingdon bank gang.

events.label: Holmes confirms the identification of Blessington as Sutton

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Exactly.

events.label: Holmes explains the Worthingdon bank case

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You must surely remember the great Worthingdon bank business. Five men were in it—these four and a fifth called Cartwright. Tobin, the caretaker, was murdered, and the thieves got away with seven thousand pounds. This was in 1875. They were all five arrested, but the evidence against them was by no means conclusive. This Blessington or Sutton, who was the worst of the gang, turned informer. On his evidence Cartwright was hanged and the other three got fifteen years apiece. When they got out the other day, some years before their full term, they set themselves to hunt down the traitor and to avenge the death of their comrade upon him. Twice they tried to get at him and failed; a third time, it came off.

events.label: The doctor says the explanation is clear

communicates.speaker: doctor
communicates.content: I think you have made it all remarkably clear.

events.label: Holmes explains Blessington's concealment

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: No doubt the day on which he was perturbed was the day when he had seen of their release in the newspapers. His talk about a burglary was the merest blind. Knowing the vindictive character of his old associates, he was trying to hide his own identity from everybody as long as he could. His secret was a shameful one, and he could not bring himself to divulge it.

events.label: Holmes states that the shield of British law may fail but justice remains

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: However, wretch as he was, he was still living under the shield of British law, and I have no doubt, Inspector, that you will see that, though that shield may fail to guard, the sword of justice is still there to avenge.

events.label: The police see nothing more of the three murderers
The proceedings against the page break down for lack of evidence

clues.significance: Holmes inferred the visitor was a general practitioner and recently established in practice from the nature and state of the medical instruments in the wicker basket.
Holmes inferred the young man's individuality from the stair-carpet prints and from the square-toed, longer shoes that differed from Blessington's and the doctor's.
Holmes inferred that the scene included signs of deliberate staging from the cigar-ends, the cigar-case, the locked door, and the body position.
Holmes inferred that the photograph of Blessington would help in his inquiries after taking it from the mantelpiece.
Holmes inferred that a wire had been used to force the key round on the locked door.
Holmes inferred that a consultation lasted some time from the cigars being smoked.
Holmes inferred that the older man used the cigar-holder from the traces in the room.
Holmes inferred that a screw-driver was used for fixing the gallows structure.
Holmes inferred that the screws were used for fixing the gallows structure.
Holmes inferred that the men saved themselves trouble by using the hook instead of setting up the gallows.
Holmes inferred that the men brought a block or pulley to serve as a gallows from the arrangement in the room.
